atomicity.reason: Two thresholds for two distinct fault mechanisms (undervoltage below 2.50 V, overvoltage above 4.25 V); each would stand alone as a complete protection requirement, though both are facets of one 'cell voltage window' obligation.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into a separate undervoltage and overvoltage requirement, matching the per-limit granularity already used for overtemperature and overcurrent.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained - the reader needs nothing else to know what is required.

feasibility.reason: Standard per-cell voltage monitoring against a static limit table; contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: Squarely addresses the parent story's voltage arm - a single cell leaving its safe voltage window disconnects the pack.

unambiguity.reason: One reading; the explicit 'regardless of the pack voltage' clause forecloses the obvious misreading.

verifiability.reason: Both limits carry values and units, the per-cell scope is explicit, and the reaction is externally observable at the contactors.

summary: Precise and testable, but it bundles undervoltage and overvoltage protection into one requirement while the comparable overtemperature and overcurrent limits each get their own.
